Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 1. Overview

Virtual Terminal is a cross-platform mobile application that lets merchant staff process gift card

transactions — loading value, redeeming purchases, checking balances and voiding transactions —

directly from an Android or iOS device.

After signing in with merchant credentials, the app retrieves the merchant profile and the list of functions

enabled for that account from the Synergy web service, and shows only those actions on the dashboard.

A card is identified by scanning its barcode with the device camera or by keying in the card number, and

every operation is confirmed on screen with a receipt that can be emailed to the customer.

The application is built on .NET 9 and .NET MAUI using the MVVM pattern. It communicates with the

Synergy web service (SynergyWebX.asmx) through SOAP/XML requests; card balances and transaction

records are held on the Synergy server, and the app keeps no local transaction database.

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 2. Business Context

Merchants that sell and accept gift cards typically need to:

• Load value onto a gift card at the time of sale

• Redeem a card against a purchase and show what is left on it

• Look up a card’s balance and recent activity on request

• Reverse (void) a transaction when a mistake has been made

• Give each merchant account only the functions it is entitled to

• Provide the customer with a receipt for every load or redemption

Virtual Terminal brings these tasks together in one mobile app connected directly to the Synergy gift and

loyalty platform, with the available functions controlled per merchant account.

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.1 Merchant Login & Access Control

• Merchants sign in with a user ID and password, which the Synergy web service validates

• The service returns the merchant profile and the list of enabled functions; if none are enabled the app
reports “No Features Enabled”

• The dashboard presents Load Gift Card, Redeem Gift Card, Void Transaction and Check Balance
according to those enabled functions

• Returning users with an active session open directly on the dashboard; Logout in the menu clears the
session

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.2 Load Gift Card

• The merchant scans or keys in the card number, then enters the amount to load; an empty amount is
rejected

• The load is processed on the Synergy server; the app confirms success or reports an invalid card
number

• The receipt shows the card number, date, amount loaded and the updated card balance

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.3 Redeem Gift Card

• The merchant enters the sale amount to redeem, with optional clerk and check number fields

• The app reports the outcome: a normal redemption, a redemption that uses the whole balance, or
insufficient funds

• When the balance is short, the amount the customer still owes is calculated and displayed and carried
onto the receipt

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.4 Balance Inquiry & Recent Transactions

• Merchants scan or key in a card to see its current balance

• The card’s recent transactions are listed with their date and reference number

• A Transactions screen lists transactions for a selected date, showing authorization number, date, time
and gross amount

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.5 Void Transaction

• The merchant picks a date to list transactions; entries without a card number or authorization number
are skipped

• Selecting a transaction opens its details: card number, authorization number, merchant, date and
gross amount

• Voiding requires the login password to be re-entered; on success the app confirms “Void Successful”
and returns to the transaction list

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.6 Card Capture: Barcode Scan & Key-In

• The camera scanner reads any supported barcode format and strips dashes and spaces from the
value

• The value must be numeric; the scanned number is shown for confirmation with Next or Retry, and a
successful scan gives haptic feedback

• A Key in Card Number option lets the merchant type the number instead; the flow then continues to
the load, redeem or balance screen that started it

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.7 Receipts & Email Delivery

• After a load or redemption, a receipt screen shows the card number, date, amount, card balance, clerk
and check number

• Email Receipt accepts one or more comma-separated addresses, validates each, and shows “Invalid
Email” when none are valid

• The HTML email masks the card number to its last four digits and uses separate subjects for loads
and redemptions

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.8 Help, Feedback & About

• Help & Support opens the Synergy support website in an in-app web view

• Feedback lets the user type a message and send it by email, and displays the company’s contact
details

• About shows the application name and version information

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 6. System Architecture & Integrations

The app is organized in layers and connects to a small number of external services:

• Presentation: XAML pages for sign-in, dashboard, card scan, load, redeem, card balance,
transactions, void details, receipt, help, feedback and about, inside a Shell flyout menu

• View models: MVVM view models with bindable state and commands, resolved through dependency
injection

• Service repositories: card (balance, load, redeem), login and void services, each building a SOAP
envelope and posting it to the web service

• Synergy web service: SynergyWebX.asmx over HTTPS — credentials, load, redeem, balance
inquiry, void and transaction reports; JSON results returned inside the XML reply and parsed with
Newtonsoft.Json

• Email: customer receipts and feedback messages sent through an SMTP relay (Amazon SES, port
587, SSL)

• Device services: camera for barcode capture, haptic feedback, and Preferences / SecureStorage for
session data

Platform
.NET 9 and .NET MAUI (C#) — Android & iOS

Supported OS
Android 5.0+ (API 21) and iOS 12.2+

Application Design
MVVM with CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, dependency injection, Shell navigation with

Backend Services
Synergy web service (SynergyWebX.asmx) accessed with SOAP/XML requests;
JSON responses parsed with Newtonsoft.Json

Card Scanning
ZXing.Net.MAUI, BarcodeScanner.Mobile.Maui and Camera.MAUI

User Interface
XAML views, CommunityToolkit.Maui, Controls.UserDialogs.Maui (dialogs, toasts,
loading), XCalendar.Maui, Material Icons and Open Sans fonts

Local Storage
.NET MAUI Preferences and SecureStorage; no local database

Email
System.Net.Mail SMTP client on port 587 with SSL and an HTML receipt template

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 8. Security & Data Handling

• Sign-in credentials are validated by the Synergy web service; the app does not keep a local user
directory

• The merchant key returned at sign-in is held in platform SecureStorage; logout clears it, the stored
password and the session flag

• Voiding a transaction requires the user to re-enter the login password

• Available functions are restricted per merchant account, based on the features enabled on the
Synergy platform

• Web service requests use an HTTPS endpoint, and receipt email is sent over SMTP with SSL enabled

• Emailed receipts show only the last four digits of the card number

• Card balances and transaction history stay on the Synergy server; the app keeps no local transaction
database

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 9. Value Delivered

• Turns a phone or tablet into a gift card terminal for loading, redeeming, balance checks and voids

• Speeds up card handling with barcode scanning and validated card-number entry

• Keeps each merchant in control: an account only sees the functions it is entitled to

• Reduces errors with clear on-screen outcomes, including the amount owed when a card balance is
insufficient

• Gives customers an emailed receipt for every load and redemption

• Supports Android and iOS from a single .NET MAUI codebase

• Connects directly to the existing Synergy web service and stores no transaction data on the device
